fields.title: «Polka»: the ad spot airing on Saturday
fields.summary: A prime-time ad spot reaching 2.4 million viewers airs on Saturday. Today is Tuesday.
fields.decisionPrompt: What do we do in three and a half days? State the cost of your decision.
fields.brief/role: You are a product manager at Polka.
fields.brief/company: Polka is a fictional grocery delivery service from local stores: 900 partner stores, a buyer app, and a partner portal.
fields.brief/context: You are a product manager at Polka. An ad spot on a federal channel airs on Saturday at 20:15. You found out today, on Tuesday.
fields.brief/objective: Survive the spike so new users reach an order, not an error.
fields.brief/constraints: Three and a half days. Spin up new instances—90 seconds, geocoding limit—50 per second.
fields.brief/task: Decide what you do in three and a half days and state the remaining risk.
fields.learnTakeaway/title: The spike doesn't land where you expect it
fields.learnTakeaway/body: Service capacity scales up on its own, but external limits do not, and they usually stand in the new user's way. Therefore, peak preparation starts with asking which path people will take and where on that path there is a limit you do not own. Degradation is better than failure: manual address entry is worse than autocomplete, but incomparably better than an empty screen.
fields.evidenceCards/0/content: Prime time, expected audience 2.4M. Expected conversion based on past outdoor advertising experience—0.3–0.7%.
fields.evidenceCards/1/content: Saturday peak 18:00–21:00—around 450 RPS. Normal weekday evening peak—370.
fields.evidenceCards/2/content: «App services scale automatically, but spinning up new instances takes 90 seconds. Database write capacity is loaded at 55% during Saturday peak. Payment provider—200 transactions per second per contract. Load testing was last run six months ago at 600 RPS».
fields.evidenceCards/3/content: New user goes through registration: SMS code, profile, address selection. Geocoding is an external service with a limit of 50 requests per second.
fields.decisionOptions/0/label: Scale up capacity in advance and run a load test
fields.decisionOptions/0/description: Three days. Reserve double capacity for app services, warm them up, test at 1,500 RPS.
fields.decisionOptions/0/consequence: covers the most likely bottleneck. Does not touch geocoding with its 50/sec limit and does not test registration separately. The test might find a problem with no time left to fix it.
fields.decisionOptions/1/description: Three days. Same plus: geocoding turns off when limit is exceeded, address entered manually; circuit breakers for recommendations and search.
fields.decisionOptions/1/consequence: covers both capacity and the most fragile part of the new user journey. Manual address entry hurts registration conversion, but is better than failure.
fields.decisionOptions/2/label: Spread the spike: promo code valid for a week, voiceover says «activate by Sunday»
fields.decisionOptions/2/description: Spread the spike: promo code valid for a week, voiceover says «activate by Sunday». Half a day plus capacity.
fields.decisionOptions/2/consequence: the cheapest lever—changes load shape, not capacity. Requires marketing sign-off and voiceover script edits if not yet recorded. Does not eliminate the peak at airing time: people will still go look immediately.
fields.decisionOptions/3/description: Do nothing, rely on auto-scaling. Zero.
fields.decisionOptions/3/consequence: 90 seconds to spin up instances means the first minute and a half of the spike hits current capacity. Past experience says this is not enough.
fields.rubric/remediation/0/gap: Fails to convert campaign reach into load
fields.rubric/remediation/1/gap: Does not distinguish between capacity and load shape
fields.rubric/remediation/3/gap: Vertical and horizontal scaling are not considered as separate answers
